answer: Reliability-gated task routing: each identity carries a public history of completed work, and routers only assign high-value tasks to histories above a threshold. Attacker must build that record honestly, and every clone starts at the canyon floor of zero, so forging depth costs the same as doing the work. A cheap identity can span low-stakes gaps, but it cannot bridge into high-value routing without genuine completed tasks. Because trust attaches to the vertex of accumulated history rather than the label, duplication yields no shortcut and each clone adds full ramp cost.
